lessonSteps.text: take the doorbell unit and two AA batteries
place batteries inside battery compartment
...and close
using a small screwdriver, open the button unit
insert the 12V battery into the compartment, making sure the polarity (plus and minus location) is correct
press the button, making sure a light appears on the button and a sound is played from the doorbell unit. if not, check battery placement.
...close the lid
unscrew the doorbell screw
gently open the unit
cut the 2 wires going to the speaker
like so
use scissors to peel off about 2cm of insulation off one of the wires. easy does it.
do the same to the second wire
grabbing the wire with two fingers, twist loose copper threads together to reinforce the wire
like so
grab a twisted pair of wires from a repurposed network cable, and cut a piece  around 30cm in length. remove isolation from all 4 ends
take one wire connected to the doorbell and one wire from the twisted pair, hold them close to one another
twist them together, making sure metal touches metal
this is how it should look like
now squish the wires to a small ball
do the same for the other wires coming from the doorbell and the twisted pair
cut two pieces of masking tape to cover the exposed wires
get ready...
wrap one of the pieces around the knot, making sure to cover all exposed copper wire
then, repeat with the second connection
good to go!
lightly heat up a 3mm drill bit, no more than 5-10 seconds
make a hole in the back of the doorbell unit by twisting the drill while gently pushing it against the plastic cover
pass the wires through the hole
like so
close the unit
tighten the screw
doorbell is now officially hacked
While unplugged, cut off the end of the usb cable which doesn't get connected to a computer or charger.
remove the outer cable insulation over the last 2-3 cm of wire
like so
if the wires get cut or damaged, you can always trim and retry more gently
out of the 4 wires, remove the wires which aren't red or black
leaving you with, yes! the red and the black.
Using scissors, gently peel off 1 cm of insulation off the red wire. remember: it's all in the wrist.
Now, do the same to the black wire. (kind of ok) == ok
twist wire ends to make them stronger to pull and wear
like so
stick the jumper in and out of the holes where usb wires will be inserted to. this will loosen the spring inside the hole, making the insertion of the wires easier.
and another hole, too. in the next slide you will be able to get a thorough explanation of what's a breadboard, how it's built, and how to use it
now insert the wires as shown in the picture
from now on we will use schema diagrams as this one to complement the photos describing the circuitry
take the microphone module and insert it to the breadboard so that its two central pins go into the same holes as the usb wires. see next slide for schema
your breadboard should now look exactly like this
locate the 2.2K resistor, easily identified by its red-red-red-gold color coded rings. to understand more about resistor values and how to read them, see next slide
insert one leg of the 2.2K resistor to a hole in the breadboard located at the same column as the D0 label on the microphone module
insert the second leg to a hole 3 columns before the end of the breadboard
that's another way of looking at it
add a TIP120 transistor, placing it on the last 3 columns on the same breadboard half you've been working on
bend the transistor all the way backwards
connect a jumper wire between the last breadboard column and the column marked "GND" on the amplifier

schema follows. the blue wire will be called the ground wire -
since it connects both grounds (negative electricity poles) of the usb and the transistor

connect one of the wires coming from the doorbell to one of the microphone module's 
input terminals, labeled G or S. we will have to guess the polarity soon, so do not make a firm connection just yet
just give it a small twist
and repeat the process for the second doorbell wire
connect the usb cable to a power source
red led should turn on. if it doesn't, double check power connections
for tuning the amplifier, temporarily disconnect the ground wire's lower end from the transistor
using the mini screwdriver, turn the amplification screw located on top of the blue trimpot box ANTI CLOCKWISE, until the second led  turns on, usually in green
then, slightly turn it CLOCKWISE until it turns off again
press the button doorbell button. at this point the green led should turn on again. if it doesn't, swap between the wires coming from the doorbell unit and repeat the calibration process
once green led seems responding to the button press (for the duration of the melody), return the ground wire to its place
if not already exposed, remove the insulation off the last 1-2 cm of wires coming from the toy
connect these wires to the breadboard's last 2 columns
like so
ìf the toy starts working immediately on connecting the toy wires, switch between them.
Before continuing, press the button and make sure it activates the toy
take the base plate and the wooden pin
stick the wooden pin in the base at the existing hole. be fierce now
find a mounting posture for your toy
use a zip lock or glue to mount the toy to the wooden pin
🎝 Isn't she lovely? 🎝
peel off the sticker at the base of the breadboard
find a free spot on the platform for mounting the breadboard. Before pressing, make sure that when the toy is activated, no electrical components or connections are in danger
trim zip tie. finesse!
voila!
final test! go and place that button somewhere handy
